name: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

date.note: Preprint submission date; the PRL publication (108, 171803) followed in April 2012.

title: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

claim.quote: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

summary.plain: Daya Bay found clear proof that electron antineutrinos from nuclear reactors change into another type over a distance of about a kilometre, pinning down the last unmeasured neutrino mixing angle.
summary.technical: Using six antineutrino detectors at near (470 m, 576 m) and far (1648 m) halls and a 43,000 ton-GW_th-day exposure over 55 days, Daya Bay measured a deficit R = 0.940 ± 0.011(stat) ± 0.004(syst) in the far-to-near ratio, establishing sin²(2θ₁₃) ≠ 0 at 5.2σ.

why_it_matters.value: Measured a non-zero value for the neutrino mixing angle theta_13, the least known of the three mixing angles before this result, with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations.
why_it_matters.quote: The Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment has measured a non-zero value for the neutrino mixing angle θ13 with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations. ... Of these mixing angles, θ13 is the least known.
